# meshmsg v0.1.19

This release hardens persistent state, operation contracts, release controls, and daemon logging. It is focused on bounded resource use, fail-closed validation, truthful outcomes, and reliable behavior during overload, output blockage, and process failure.

## Security and reliability

- Adds schema-versioned, size-bounded persistent-state loading and crash-safe migration for configuration, aliases, attachment retention, and direct-message replay state.
- Closes persistent-state pathname races with no-follow/reparse-aware opens, regular-file checks, exact file-identity verification, atomic no-replace commits, and synchronized recovery boundaries.
- Tightens message, attachment offer, lifecycle, and error contracts with canonical bounded fields, strict operation correlation, compatibility checks, and fail-closed rejection of malformed or private diagnostics.
- Completes attachment mutation idempotency and preserves explicit `accepted`, `not_started`, and `unknown` outcome semantics across queue saturation, timeouts, shutdown, and partial completion.
- Makes daemon stdout and diagnostic logging bounded and nonblocking. Slow or broken output consumers no longer stall daemon work or teardown; loss, contention, queue peaks, and terminal writer health are reported separately and truthfully.
- Contains panics at top-level process and output-worker boundaries, restores scoped panic hooks, and emits bounded canonical terminal diagnostics.

## Verification and releases

- Introduces one reusable exact-SHA verification workflow for pull requests, protected `main`, and release tags, with stable required-check aggregation.
- Adds native Windows verification, a complete budgeted Linux integration inventory, dependency policy gates, workflow mutation tests, and release metadata/archive adversarial tests.
- Hardens release admission and publication with immutable/tag-authority rules, protected-main ancestry checks, live policy audits, exact-SHA release notes, inspected GNU/musl/static-CRT Windows archives, and unified checksums.

## Compatibility

Persistent state may be migrated to current schema versions during startup. Stop all meshmsg processes before upgrading, keep generated rollback backups, and upgrade/restart all daemons, CLI clients, and web processes together. Unsupported, corrupt, redirected, oversized, or identity-mismatched state now fails closed rather than being guessed or partially accepted.

Install this exact source release:

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/Eldar-Ahmadov/meshmsg \
  --tag v0.1.19 --locked --force
```

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/Eldar-Ahmadov/meshmsg/compare/v0.1.18...v0.1.19
